body:
- **Slug:** split-children-inherit-release-metadata
- **Defect / goal:** `pdca split --accept` files each child with a title, a body and
  `--parent`, and nothing else. `_create_issue` (`split.py:580-607`) builds exactly:

  ```
  gh issue create --repo <repo> --title <title> --body <body> [--parent <n>]
  ```

  `split.py` contains no reference to `milestone`, `label` or `assignee` at all. So the
  moment a slice is decomposed — the moment its work moves from one tracker item to
  several — every piece of release-planning metadata the parent carried is silently
  dropped, and the children land unmilestoned and unlabelled.

  The milestone is the loss that matters. A milestone is how release scope is counted, and
  a split is precisely when the count needs to follow the work. It does not, so the counter
  stops describing reality in **both** directions at once: the parent stays open in the
  milestone until its close cycle runs, while the children doing its actual work are
  invisible to it. Merged children do not register as progress; live children do not
  register as remaining scope.

  Observed on `getwyrd/wyrd` milestone **0.1 Alpha** (2026-08-08). Three parents split into
  eight children, every one filed with `milestone=NONE`:

  | parent (0.1 Alpha) | children | state |
  |---|---|---|
  | #654 | 691, 692, 693 | 691 merged; 692, 693 open |
  | #681 | 695, 696, 697 | all three merged |
  | #682 | 710, 711 | both open |

  The milestone read **38 open / 17 closed**. Four merged slices (691, 695, 696, 697) were
  absent from the closed count and four live ones (692, 693, 710, 711) absent from the open
  count — a quarter of the milestone's real content missing while #681, whose every child
  had merged, still counted as outstanding work. Assigning the eight by hand moved it to
  **42 open / 21 closed**. Nothing detected this; it was noticed only while planning a batch.

  Labels go the same way and are worth fixing in the same pass: #681 and #682 are
  `enhancement`, and #695, #710, #711 carry no labels at all.

- **Success criterion:**

  (a) A child issue filed by `--accept` **inherits the parent's milestone** when the parent
      has one, via `gh issue create --milestone`. Verified against the tracker, not just the
      argv: the eight children above would have needed no manual fix.

  (b) It inherits the parent's **labels** the same way.

  (c) A parent with no milestone or no labels adds **no flag** — the child is filed exactly
      as today. Inheritance never invents metadata the parent did not carry.

  (d) Reading the parent's metadata is **best-effort and never fatal**. A `gh issue view`
      that fails, times out, or returns something unparseable must leave the child filed
      *without* the metadata and say so on stderr — not abort the batch. Tracker issues
      cannot be rolled back, so a metadata lookup must never be the thing that strands a
      half-filed set of children (the `UncertainFiling` path in `_create_issue` exists
      because this batch is already the least reversible step in the driver). Fetch the
      parent's metadata **once**, before the filing loop, not per child.

  (e) The `--ids` path and any non-GitHub tracker are unaffected: those children already
      exist and the driver files nothing.

  (f) **Offline test**, no `gh`: with a stubbed issue-creation call, a parent carrying a
      milestone and labels produces argv containing `--milestone` and `--label`; a bare
      parent produces neither; and a failing metadata lookup still files every child and
      warns. Assert on the argv and on the child set, so a regression cannot pass by
      silently filing fewer children.

- **Test file:** tests/test_split_child_metadata.py

- **Difficulty:** low

## Deliberately not in scope

**Assignees.** Who works a child is a fresh decision, not an inheritance — a parent assigned
to one person does not mean each of its N slices is theirs. Copying that is likelier wrong
than right, and unlike a milestone it is not a counting error.

**Retroactive backfill** of children filed before the fix. Instance data; the eight above are
already corrected by hand.

**Closing the parent.** Separate concern: a split parent stays open in its milestone until
its own close cycle runs, and `publish` deliberately leaves the tracker item to the human
("nothing to contribute; close the tracker item by hand"). Inheriting the milestone makes the
double-count visible and short-lived rather than permanent, which is enough here.

## Notes

Found while planning a 0.1 Alpha batch, alongside #466 (stub splitter reaching the tracker).
Both are the same shape of gap — `--accept` is the driver's least reversible step and the
least guarded — but they are independent: #466 is about *whether* the children should be
filed, this is about *what they are filed as*.
title: split --accept files children with no milestone and no labels — a split drops the parent's release metadata
